WAR-ROOM v16.37

1V1 DEATH BATTLES • ENGINE v16.37 • TEXT BREAKDOWN FIRST • NO RESEARCH STAT BONUS

Phase 3 — simplified flow

Pick two fighters, battle, read the breakdown — that is the whole flow in v16.37. History, export, read-aloud, Advanced Settings, and live-research retests are removed in this build; the breakdown page is the result. Search and category filters, the Review Matchup edge table, the collapsed Audit disclosure (with Combat Details inside), and dossier Info are kept.

1 — Search & Browse the Roster

This build ships 194 playable fighters across 6 categories (Anime 33, Comics 33, Video Games 32, Movies & TV 32, Animation 32, Fantasy & Sci-Fi 32). The next-batch target is 100 per category — that is a target, not a claim. The roster is NOT 600 fighters; do not treat the target as implemented. Each card uses an emoji fallback portrait so no image ever breaks. Real artwork is not included.

Combat Roster

2 — Death (knockout) Match: Pick Fighter A and Fighter B

1v1 only. Pick exactly two fighters — one for each side. Both fighters are chosen by you — WAR-ROOM is 1v1 only.

Mirror matches are blocked in this build: the same fighter cannot fight itself. In Death mode a knockout is never labelled death. In Incapacitation mode a knockout is labelled unconscious, not dead. Surrender and escape are not simulated outcomes in this build — the verdict will not claim them.

RESULT

Online breakdown status

Online breakdown status appears here during and after generation.

Death (knockout) Battle Breakdown

The main breakdown below is a resolver telling: it is generated from the schema resolver frozen result (winner, reason, finisher, loser state, word-only exchanges, transforms with triggers met), locked to that result, and it states no HP numbers, damage totals, or round counts. While online generation runs, the labelled offline resolver telling is shown first and replaced by the online AI breakdown when it passes validation. If online generation is unavailable, the offline resolver telling stays and is labelled honestly as offline — it is never presented as online AI. The HP engine still runs every battle, but only as a hidden audit: its numbers and round record live in the Audit disclosure below, never in the main telling.

Audit — resolver main vs HP audit, numbers, and working detail (collapsed by default; numbers live here, not in the main telling)

The resolver is the main output in this build: it reads the schema records and decides the winner, reason, finisher, and loser state for the main telling. The HP engine still runs every battle, but only as a hidden audit — its result, numbers, and round record live in this Audit disclosure, and the audit panel below reports MATCH when all four fields agree with the resolver, or PARTIAL with the differences listed honestly. A winner disagreement is stated plainly as a winner disagreement, never buried. PARTIAL is honest, not a failure: it means the two systems explain the same battle differently.

Audit comparison appears here after the battle — it is hidden inside this collapsed disclosure by default. If the comparison cannot be computed, the reason is shown here, never nothing.
